thread_title: S. leucophylla hurricane creek white  clone A
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla hurricane creek white  clone A

posts.body_html:
As some of you may recall in a previous thread, S. leucophylla Hurricane Creek White clone A is a very mysterious plant (as are all the HCW clones in the collection). For one, the pitchers on the same exact clone can look completely different from one plant to the next. Sometimes, it produces pinkish pigments below the mouth of in pitchers, and at other times, it's pure white. The shape of the pitchers can vary as well.

Here are some recent pictures of spring pitchers. The fall pitchers will look almost completely different and are typically solid white.


All pictures are from one clone, S. leucophylla Hurricane Creek White clone A, Baldwin Co, AL:








The color here is so drastically different, it looks like a completely different clone. Notice how the green veins are more pronounced in this individual plant. However, this is still clone A!:

posts.body_html:
Got this beauty from Mike last winter and here it is as of a couple days ago. It's fall pitchers have come on gradually - it put out a couple nice 22-24" traps a couple weeks ago and I was like, "sweet fall pitchers" but then it pumped out the 28" monster on the right, with two more good sized traps following on behind. I know it could get even bigger in coming seasons! 

Close up of the big guy
